correctness.rationale: Cubical coordinate complements send the marked p to origin, leaving exactly C(15,4)=1365 tetrahedron vertex subsets. I independently enumerated all 4-column rank tests over the rationals, 940 full-dimensional cases, and minimized squared norm on all 15 faces by solving rational barycentric projection systems and checking nonnegative weights. Exactly one fixed-p candidate has distance squared 1/4; 28 have 1/3; no intermediate level; the third shell begins at 2/5. The 28 second candidates form three coordinate-permutation orbits of sizes 12,12,4; multiplying by 16 marked p gives 448 global cases and orbits 192,192,64. This exhaustive independent finite certificate is complete because all subsets and convex faces are considered; not empirical extrapolation.
